papers.title: Ohmic warm inflation
papers.abstract: We show that Warm Little Inflation is anomalous, lacks a suitable inflaton potential, and cannot sustain the thermal bath, as the quasi-static approximation over-estimated the dissipated power. To address these issues, we propose a new friction mechanism and new anomaly-free models based on one fermion charged under a U(1) gauge group in one extra dimension. papers.title: Is Neutrino Disappearance Sensitive to T-Violation for Asymmetric Matter Profiles ?
papers.abstract: It is commonly stated in the literature that T violation is zero in neutrino disappearance channels. We show this claim is not general: it holds only for symmetric matter profiles or when the T/CP-violating phase ($δ$) is 0 or $π$, that is, when the Jarlskog invariant is zero. The $ν_μ$ and $ν_τ$, but not the $ν_e$, survival probabilities carry a $\sinδ$-dependent term that is non-zero in asymmetric matter and constitutes a genuine T asymmetry. papers.title: On the non-uniqueness of solutions of the axi-symmetric swirl-free Navier-Stokes equations, II
papers.abstract: We prove optimal non-uniqueness of Leray solutions of the unforced incompressible Navier-Stokes equations in 3D within the class of axially symmetric swirl-free flows. More precisely, we construct two solutions $u_1,u_2$ that have the same initial data $u_1(0)=u_2(0)$, are smooth for every positive time, satisfy the energy identity, and satisfy \[ u_1,u_2\in C_tH_x^α\cap L_t^2H_x^{α+1}\,\,\text{ for every }\,\,0\leqα<1/2,\qquad u_1,u_2\in L_t^\infty L_x^{3,\infty}\cap L_t^{2,\infty}L_x^\infty

papers.title: Quantum Many-Body Scars from Operator Size
papers.abstract: We present a general construction of approximate many-body scar states in two copies of a system using a bilocal size interaction that couples one site to its partner on the other copy. For an uncoupled two-sided Hamiltonian whose terms have fixed size in an operator basis, we identify polynomially many Krylov basis states that it annihilates and that, in the thermodynamic limit, become concentrated on a single size sector. papers.title: Observation of rotonic density enhancement at the boundary of a uniform dipolar superfluid
papers.abstract: The collective excitations of a quantum liquid lie at the heart of its emergent behaviour. In many systems, the variation of excitation energy ${\varepsilon}$ with wavevector $k$ exhibits a softening at a characteristic lengthscale, which plays a key role in thermodynamics and transport.
